svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.25.3.3 Continuity of the Air Barrier System
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.25 HEAT TRANSFER, AIR LEAKAGE AND CONDENSATION CONTROL
Continuity of the Air Barrier System

g.text: Panel joints sealed, (1). Sheet joints sealed
Interior wall meets an exterior wall: the air
Interior wall at an exterior wall
Interior wall through a ceiling: spaces in the
Floor through an exterior wall: air barrier
Penetrations such as doors, windows, wiring,
Hatches and sump pit covers weatherstripped,

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where the air barrier system consists of an air-impermeable
panel-type material, all joints are sealed to prevent air leakage.
Except as provided in Sentence 9.25.3.6.(3), where the air barrier
system consists of flexible sheet material, all joints are
(a) sealed, or (b) lapped not less than 100 mm (3 15/16″) and clamped,
such as between framing members, furring or blocking, and rigid panels.
Where an interior wall meets an exterior wall, ceiling, floor or
roof required to be provided with air barrier protection, the air
barrier system extends across the intersection.
Where an interior wall projects through a ceiling or extends to
become an exterior wall, spaces in the wall are blocked to provide
continuity across those spaces with the air barrier system in the
abutting walls or ceiling.
Where an interior floor projects through an exterior wall or
extends to become an exterior floor, continuity of the air barrier
system is maintained from the abutting walls across the floor
assembly.
Penetrations of the air barrier system, such as those created by
the installation of doors, windows, electrical wiring, electrical
boxes, piping or ductwork, are sealed to maintain the integrity of
the air barrier system over the entire surface.
Where access hatches and sump pit covers are installed through
assemblies constructed with an air barrier system, they are
weatherstripped around their perimeters to prevent air leakage.
Clearances between chimneys or gas vents and the surrounding
construction that would permit air leakage from within the building
into a wall or attic or roof space are sealed by noncombustible
material to prevent such leakage.
Drawn: red dashed lines mark seals, blue lines the air barrier, blue arrows air flow. C and D are cut between framing members. E shows two of the listed penetrations. Layouts are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.25.3.3. (page 9-235)
